entries.clue: The dark quarter of the year, when ponds harden and days shrink.
Glassy spike growing downward from a dripping eave in a freeze.
Calm blue shallows a coral reef walls off from the open sea
Dawn's thin white veil over the fields, too light to be called fog.
Treeless northern plain whose subsoil never thaws, however long the daylight
Drifting slab of frozen sea a beset ship may be pinned among
Shackleton's barquentine, crushed and sunk in the Weddell Sea in 1915
Far north named for the Bear overhead, where the pole sits on drifting ice
Bowl left behind where a volcano blew or a meteorite struck
What David is in marble and Liberty is in copper
Wasting sickness of long voyages, held off by fresh meat and lemons
